A distinctive culture developed in the Appalachian South by the early 1800's, typified mainly by a preservation of archaic traits, including the persistence of a frontier way of life. You would need a lot more of a rigorous linguistic library in order to track cultural elements. It's not simply "pop vs. Soda", but accents as well as vocabulary. This has decreased over time due to centralization of population and public education normalizing vocabulary, for segments of the U.S. and sometimes whole states were populated by immigrants from Ireland, Germany, the Netherlands, etc. The reason why it's not indicative with these terms alone is because there are actually more accent variations than there are variations of names for Soda.

Although it's your basic heat map, here is an example of one such study from a survey. As you can see, certain dialectical trends are quite indicative of a lot of cultural diversity within the U.S. This cultural diversity is, also, part of the reason our government can be so nonfunctional.
